hypothesis: When one major crypto closes far above its completed New York Monday range and another closes far below its own range, their relative strength can persist. Trade a dollar-neutral long/short spread so gains require the strong coin to outperform the weak one.
entry: At each completed UTC 12H after each fully observed NY Monday, measure (close - Monday midpoint)/(Monday high-low) separately per coin. With at least four observed and at least 50 consecutive 12H for each EMA, take the strongest positive candidate whose EMA20>EMA50 and weakest negative candidate whose EMA20<EMA50. Require the spread in normalized readings to be at least 2.236 (the distance between the original 1.618 outer levels). First such closed key per NY week, one live pair, enter both at the coincident observed H1 open. No entry when either quote is missing; no same-boundary exit/re-entry.
exit: Close both at first common H1 open after a completed 12H where the observed close ratio (long/short) falls at least 6% below its signal ratio, or its EMA20 falls below EMA50; maximum 28 days. A missing held H1 forces close at first next mutually observed opening with a data-gap flag. Last observation at the frozen end of tape is explicitly marked.
account: 1000 USDT, one pair fully collateralized, both legs start with equal raw-price nominal value and combined nominal exposure near 1x NAV. Taker 0.05% per entry and exit on each actual leg. Separate adverse 0.05% market-fill slippage case. An economic trade is a completed pair. Actual monetary payoff is mean winning pair cash / absolute mean losing pair cash. Funding omitted in this first mechanism screen.
control: For each original first weekly trigger clock retain the positive aligned and negative aligned candidate side pools. Draw one per side uniformly with seeds 1029 through 1033, preserving timestamp and side availability; each selected pair manages its own exits and slot. Report identities changed, pair count, development through 2024, 2025 and 2026. The ten-name basket is a fixed list of surviving majors, with different data starts; this is not an all-exchange census.
